title: Two-rank fixed-path cohesive force and portable restart
purpose: Prove that disconnected split-interface traces can be coupled without duplicated force or rank-local state identity, and that the accepted Explicit state can change MPI rank count.
physics: Two-dimensional Mode-I bilinear cohesive interface in finite-strain Explicit dynamics

execution.evidence: Three interface facets cross two disconnected bulk partitions; two ranks write the partial transient and one rank continues it.

observables: Global equal-and-opposite interface force and exact integrated positive-side resultant.
Global cohesive stored energy and one physical owner per facet.
Identical structured Explicit energy history on every rank.
One-rank restarted displacement and irreversible maximum-opening state relative to an uninterrupted reference.
acceptance: The total cohesive force is zero to 1e-12 absolute and the positive-side resultant equals strength times reference interface length.
The global stored energy equals the exact elastic triangular area at peak opening.
Every physical facet appears exactly once in the distributed snapshot.
Two-rank-to-one-rank continuation matches displacement and cohesive history to 1e-11 relative.
limitations: Dense collective exchange is a correctness reference, not a scalability result.
The benchmark covers blocked P1 displacement, two-node 2D facets, and Mode I only.
It does not validate the JMPS/Science crack-speed observations or a full thin-three-dimensional crack.
